narrative: Row-level security failures recurred three times across dashboards and report builder despite each ticket being closed as resolved; by August the customer states 'This is the third time I'm raising a data access control problem' and mentions informing legal. The final ticket describes the report builder crashing mid-save and wiping the RLS configuration entirely, with an explicit demand for 'compensation or a meaningful account credit.' A security-adjacent issue was never actually fixed, and it is now compounded by financial demands and legal awareness.

A routine timezone question was followed roughly a year later by an unannounced connector outage the customer only noticed from stale data, then a terse complaint about a 'third break this year' demanding a technical review rather than another patch. The very next ticket, a week later, is a calm API documentation question, suggesting the reliability concern was addressed rather than left to fester. No recurrence of the same fault is documented after the review was requested.

Three tickets over six months, all informational or growth-oriented: pagination clarification, a rate-limit increase request as usage grew, and a distribution-list scheduling question. No faults, no repeat contacts, no friction of any kind — a quiet, healthy account expanding its use of the API and report builder.

After a proactive best-practice question, the account hit a dashboard crash during year-end close and worked around it by 'building the year-end view in Excel from raw exports' rather than trusting the fix, adding that it is 'still working from the Excel version I built as a stopgap' when the same dataset then failed to export. By February the customer treats a dropped alert as low priority, quietly sets a personal calendar reminder instead of chasing support, and closes with 'not treating this as urgent... wanted it logged.' This is the quiet-resignation pattern: shrinking asks, self-built workarounds, and declining trust that fixes will hold.

High-volume account (12 tickets in four months) with two threads that never actually close: the original Monday export-delivery fault ('still does not work consistently... we have not changed anything') has no confirmed fix after June 4, and nightly API 429 errors recur three times ('Last month's fix didn't hold. Real explanation, please, not another patch') with the team resorting to manually re-running pulls each morning. Multiple staff (Marit and others) are filing tickets, and tone hardens over the summer even as unrelated bugs get fixed quickly.

Light touch across nine months: a routine key rotation, an intermittent formula error ('#ERROR intermittently... one run in five') that was never followed up on either way, and then a growth request to connect a new subsidiary. The unchased formula bug is a minor open thread, but the subsequent expansion ask indicates continued investment in the platform rather than disengagement.

Sparse, patient traffic: a sandbox question, an export size-limit issue, and a courteous holiday follow-up ('Understand things may be slower over the holidays but wanted to check it hadn't been missed') that got resolved. The final ticket is an unanswered feature question about multi-threshold alerts rather than a fault — low stakes, no sign of strain.

Dashboards break repeatedly across a full year — slow loads, config loss after an update, inverted alerts, missing axis labels, wrong scheduling, broken share links, wrong comparison periods — and by May the customer states 'My team has largely stopped relying on the dashboards because the filters do not hold' and demands escalation 'to someone who can actually fix it,' explicitly invoking the Professional-tier price paid. Later tickets show fatigue rather than anger ('I am not going to enumerate all the context at this point — you have the history. Please just fix it'), and a user-invite bug took 22 days to resolve. The core product this account pays for has never stabilised.

Consistently warm account: an unprompted 'Really liking the platform so far' on a cosmetic request, mild patience with turnaround times ('just took a bit longer than expected... otherwise smooth process'), and the most recent tickets are thanks for a delivered feature plus a small enhancement suggestion and a routine seat addition. Engagement is growing, not shrinking, and every recent contact is positive in tone.

Purely professional, growth-oriented traffic over nine months — multi-region connectors, SSO migration, export automation, regional permissions, a webhook follow-up, and an API-versioning question. No faults reported at all; this reads as an account expanding its footprint on the platform.

Very high-volume, consistently urgent account spanning admin, connectors, alerts, exports, dashboards and API — nearly every ticket is a same-day fire ('need this fixed today') and every one is closed within 1-2 days. Some faults recur (an alert threshold that reset to default overnight 'second time this year,' and admin rights stripped from two different users on consecutive days), and one ticket explicitly asks to 'escalate,' but the pattern throughout is fast, reliable fixes rather than abandonment — a demanding, deeply embedded user base staying engaged, not one heading for the door.

Similar profile to the account above: dense, blunt, urgent traffic across 23 tickets over 15 months, and every single one is resolved within 1-2 days. A few faults do recur — the connector goes 'out of sync again' months after a January incident, the report builder crashes and loses work twice in one quarter, and admin rights get stripped from two people on back-to-back days — but the team keeps returning with new users, new issues and routine requests rather than pulling back, consistent with a heavy, entrenched user base rather than one drifting away.

Light, calm traffic: a drill-down bug and a UI question resolved quickly, an export missing its header row that was never confirmed fixed, and then a request to add a second bank-feed connector — a growth signal that follows directly after the open issue, suggesting it wasn't serious enough to slow the account down.

Five threads are genuinely open at the point the data ends: a bulk export that fails at 60% recurs identically in February and June ('Same bulk export failure as February... Need a real fix this time'), dashboard slowness is raised a third time in July with 'it is hard to keep asking the team to be patient when the same problem keeps coming back,' a permission error blocks the account admin from deactivating users, API throttling hits well below the documented limit, and dashboard widgets go blank across all browsers with no resolution recorded. By August the customer states plainly: 'we have multiple open issues with no clear timelines. I would like to understand when these will be resolved.' Nothing here is loud, but nothing is actually fixed either.

Four well-spaced, professional tickets over eight months on an Enterprise account — a rate-limit question, a stalled holiday sync, a seat-reassignment question, and a token-expiry issue explicitly flagged as 'not urgent, just flagging.' Every issue is resolved without recurrence and without any sign of strain.

A technically sophisticated account raising forward-looking feature requests (regex alert matching, incremental sync for a 50-million-row table, HAVING-style filtering, faster alert evaluation) alongside a handful of ordinary bugs that all get fixed without recurrence. The tone throughout is collaborative and specific rather than frustrated — this is engaged, growing usage, not friction.

Five well-spaced tickets over ten months, each a distinct bug (formula blanks, stale scheduled refresh, connector auth error, a stuck duplicate button, a silent alert) resolved without recurrence and reported in a calm, factual tone throughout. No signs of accumulating frustration.
A single informational ticket about cursor-based pagination for a connector, resolved in six days. Too little signal to indicate anything beyond a normal, healthy account.

A textbook recovery arc. Repeated connector and seat-count failures through 2024-25 built to an explicit escalation in June ('I'd like this escalated to someone who can actually own it end to end... Please have someone senior call me') and a further escalated dashboard failure in July. That led to a real account review: the August tickets thank support for 'walking through the root cause... genuinely helpful to finally understand what was happening underneath,' confirm a billing credit, and ask to add a colleague as co-admin — an investment signal. The most recent ticket in October is calm and explicitly 'not a complaint this time.'

A cluster of connector, dashboard, alert and API failures through spring 2025 culminates in a demand to 'actually review this account rather than close tickets one at a time,' and when the connector issue recurs in September the customer is openly skeptical ('I don't want another quick patch, I want to know what's actually different this time before I trust it again'). A follow-up call with an engineer showing the sync logs changes the tone immediately: 'Dashboards are looking correct again... first time anyone's explained what was failing and why,' followed by a week of confirmed stability and routine, even slightly relieved, requests. One minor notification feature request remains open at the end.
